text.en:
Ravi saw that the Moon looked bigger near the horizon and asked, "Is it really bigger?"
He held a coin at arm's length against the Moon at both times. The coin covered the Moon the same way each time.
"It only looks bigger," he said. "I tested it myself."

Science grows when people ask questions, observe carefully, test ideas with experiments and share results. Ideas that fail a test are changed or dropped.
New tools such as the telescope and the microscope let people see what the eye cannot see and so changed science. Scientists in many countries, including India, built on each other's work over centuries.
Good scientists are curious, honest and open to being wrong. Scientific knowledge changes as better evidence arrives, and it helps us in health, farming, transport and communication.
Science grows through questions, careful observation and experiments.
New tools like the telescope and microscope show us more of the world.
Scientists share results and build on each other's work.
Scientific ideas change when better evidence arrives.

problem.en: Ravi thinks the Moon is bigger near the horizon. How can he test it?

text.en: He holds a coin at arm's length against the Moon when it is high and when it is near the horizon.
He compares how much of the Moon the coin covers.

why.en: The coin is the same both times.

text.en: It covers the same, so the Moon is not really bigger.

prompt.en: A friend says scientific ideas never change. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: They change when better evidence is found.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking science is a fixed list of facts.

points.en: Science grows by questions, observation and tests.
New tools help us discover more.
